newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade police give way to students - witnesses.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade police give way to students - witnesses.

text.p: Belgrade police on Thursday appeared to back down from a showdown with students, dismantling a cordon that protesters vowed to stand before until it was removed.
Reporters at the scene said police appeared to have received orders to leave, defusing a potentially violent confrontation with the students.
Police left one by one and headed towards buses parked in nearby streets, smiling and waving at students who cheered, clapped, threw balloons and patted them on the back.

Security forces remained in place ready for a parallel demonstration organised by the Zajedno opposition coalition and student leaders said the police could return once the Zajedno protest was under way.
Thursday marked the 53rd day of protests against the cancellation of local election results by President Slobodan Milosevic's ruling Socialists last November.
On Wednesday, Milosevic conceded that Zajedno had won in Nis, Serbia's second city, but Zajedno leaders vowed protests would continue until all their claims were met.
